title: DPRK Foreign Ministry Calls Denuclearization 'Definitively Closed,' Condemns NATO Summit
detail: An unnamed DPRK Foreign Ministry spokesperson said via KCNA that the question of North Korea's denuclearization is 'finally closed' and not subject to reconsideration, dismissing a July 8 trilateral statement by the defense chiefs of the US, South Korea and Japan reaffirming the goal of denuclearizing the Korean Peninsula. The spokesperson called the trilateral demand 'pointless,' argued the US and its allies should denuclearize first, and warned NATO members — responding to the alliance's Ankara summit — not to 'export geopolitical instability' from Europe into the Asia-Pacific.

media.caption: North Korea condemns NATO summit, says denuclearization should start with US allies

title: Kim Jong-un Convenes Rare Joint Meeting, Publicly Purges Senior Military Official for Corruption
detail: KCNA reported North Korean leader Kim Jong-un presided over a rare joint meeting of senior party, government and military officials in Pyongyang — the first such assembly Kim has summoned since taking power in 2011 — at which Pak Hui-chol, deputy director of the Korean People's Army General Political Bureau's Organization Department, was publicly condemned and punished for bribery, embezzlement, abuse of power and selling official military and government positions during his tenure. Kim called the offenses 'extra-large crimes.' Analysts said the unusually public handling of the case, in contrast to North Korea's typically secretive elite discipline, signals both a campaign to root out entrenched military corruption and a warning to other senior officials against factionalism.

media.caption: Kim Jong Un publicly condemns senior military official Pak Hui-chol for corruption at rare joint meeting
